chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Aḥmad ibn Rāshid, from one of the people of al-Madāʾin, who said:

I was a pilgrim of hajj with a companion of mine, and we came to the standing place. Then there was a young man sitting, wearing an izār and a ridāʾ, and on his feet were yellow sandals. I estimated the izār and the ridāʾ at one hundred and fifty dinars, and there was no trace of travel upon him. Then a beggar came near us, but we turned him away. So he went to the young man and asked him, and he picked up something from the ground and handed it to him. Then the beggar supplicated for him, exerted himself in the du'a, and prolonged it.

Then the young man stood up and disappeared from us. So we went up to the beggar and said to him, 'Woe to you, what did he give you?' He showed us a marked piece of gold, which we estimated at twenty mithqāls. So I said to my companion, 'Our Mawlā is with us, and we do not know.' Then we went seeking him, and we went around the whole standing place, but we were unable to find him. Then we asked everyone who had been around him from the people of Makkah and al-Madīnah, and they said, 'He is a young ʿAlawī who performs hajj every year on foot.'

key_terms.الدُّعَاءِ: supplication offered by the beggar in gratitude
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: the standing place of hajj, referring to the sacred station at ʿArafāt
key_terms.حَصَاةَ ذَهَبٍ: a piece or pebble of gold given as charity
key_terms.سَائِلٌ: a beggar or petitioner asking for charity
key_terms.عَلَوِيٌّ: a descendant of ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.مَوْلَانَا: our master, referring here to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.مِثْقَالًا: a unit of weight used to estimate the gold

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kāfī say about seeing the Imam عليه السلام during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter during hajj with a mysterious young ʿAlawī who gave charity in an extraordinary manner and then disappeared from sight. The narrator later realized that the figure was their Mawlā, presenting the report as one of the accounts of those who saw him عليه السلام. The narration highlights his generosity, hidden presence, and recurring attendance at hajj.
